summary: Cameroon's eVisa portal says you can only apply for a visa to enter Cameroon online at evisacam.cm; an approved application is followed by biometric enrolment and the visa sticker, either at the entry border post or at a Cameroonian diplomatic or consular post. The Embassy of Cameroon in Japan says a valid visa is required to enter Cameroon under Law No. 97/012 of 10 January 1997 as amended, that ordinary passport holders apply and pay exclusively through the online portal, and lists Nigeria with free movement for everybody; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens must have a visa. Under a 2013 CEMAC additional act, nationals of CEMAC member states (Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Chad) may travel without a visa and stay in another member state for up to ninety days.

tips.text: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to the North-West and South-West regions and the Far North. The UK makes exceptions around Maroua, advises against all but essential travel to Limbé, and advises against all travel to the Bakassi Peninsula and within 40km of the borders with Nigeria (except Garoua), Chad and the Central African Republic.

Cameroon's eVisa portal says you can only apply for a visa to enter Cameroon online at evisacam.cm, and that the visa sticker is affixed either at the entry border post or at the relevant diplomatic or consular post.

WHO's country list says proof of yellow fever vaccination is required for all travellers aged 1 year or over entering Cameroon, and Cameroon's eVisa portal lists international vaccination certificates among the documents for every visa category.

The UK government's travel advice says to avoid travelling at night, particularly in rural areas, that many roads are heavily potholed and unlit at night, and that police and gendarmerie roadblocks are common. It also says to always carry ID — a residence permit or a certified copy of your passport showing a valid visa — and that the police can detain you without it.

The UK government's travel advice says shops usually require small notes, which can be difficult to obtain, that ATMs are not often available outside large towns, and that euros and US dollars are the most widely accepted foreign currency.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Cameroon?
faq.answer: Nationals of CEMAC member states (the Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Chad) may travel without a visa and stay up to ninety days under the 2013 CEMAC additional act. The Embassy of Cameroon in Japan says a valid visa is required to enter Cameroon under Law No. 97/012 of 10 January 1997 as amended, and that ordinary passport holders apply and pay exclusively through the online portal; it lists Nigeria with free movement for everybody, and Mali with a visa free of charge for ordinary passport holders. The UK and Canadian governments say their citizens must have a visa. Cameroon's eVisa portal says you can only apply online at evisacam.cm, and the visa sticker is affixed at the entry border post or at a Cameroonian diplomatic or consular post.

faq.question: Does Cameroon offer a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Not without applying online first. Cameroon's eVisa portal says you must apply online; if your application is validated and there is no diplomatic representation in your country, you register on arrival at an entry point and the visa sticker is affixed to your passport there. The UK government says you cannot get a visa on arrival at Yaoundé or Douala airport, and that travellers arriving by road or sea must get a physical visa from a Cameroon embassy or high commission beforehand.

faq.question: How much does the Cameroon eVisa cost?
faq.answer: Cameroon's eVisa portal sets an administrative processing fee of 153€ for a normal short-stay visa (1 to 180 days), 229€ for a short-stay express visa, 305€ for a normal long-stay visa (181 to 360 days) and 153€ for a transit visa (4 to 30 days). It says fees may be waived for certain categories of applicants and are not refunded, even if the application is refused or withdrawn.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Cameroon?
faq.answer: Yes. WHO's country list says proof of vaccination against yellow fever is required for all travellers aged 1 year or over entering Cameroon.

faq.question: Is Cameroon safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Parts of it are not. The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to the North-West and South-West regions and the Far North region; the UK also advises against all but essential travel to Limbé and the North Region, including Garoua. Canada says violent crime occurs frequently, especially at night, in major cities and on main roads.

Visa fees are not refunded, even if the application is refused or withdrawn.
Under normal procedures, the visa is issued within 72 hours of payment of the online fee.

visaTypes.evisa-transit.feeNotes.text: 153€ for a transit visa (4 to 30 days).

If you are transiting through one of Cameroon's airports on your way to another country, border police checks are conducted at that airport. Unless your visa is waived, you are subject to a Cameroon transit visa, which may not exceed 30 days.
Under normal procedures, the visa is issued within 72 hours of payment of the online fee.
